[b]Statement from the United States of Oceanica [/b]

[spoiler=The Meeting]
11:35 AM | Wednesday, March 29, 2028
Location: Enclave Pentagon Headquarters

News Reporter
With the upcoming election on April 6, 2028, marking the next presidential term, the political climate across the United States of Oceanica continues to grow tense. The recent rise of Red Fear has sparked strong government support for the Federal Techno-Democracys efforts to prevent the spread of aggressive communism and socialism.

However, public opinion remains divided. Recent surveys show that nearly 45% of citizens disapprove of the government's involvement in the overseas conflict between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke. While officials insist that assistance remains limited to supplies and volunteers, many citizens fear deeper involvement that could escalate tensions further.

The screen fades to black.

*The President reaches forward and switches off the television.*

The room grows quiet.

The door slides open as several officials from the Enclave Representative Council enter the room meeting. 

At the head of the long briefing table sits President Ironvisak F. Willham, his expression stern.

President Ironvisak F. Willham
Did I not warn that this would lead to conflict, General Arthur? And you as well, Ms.Kimball.

Across the table stands

General John Arthur
 Mr. President With respect, we anticipated tension, yes. But the speed at which the situation escalated between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke was unexpected.

He places a folder on the table and slides it toward the President.

Satellite intelligence shows troop mobilizations along the frontier. Rosenmarkke has begun reinforcing navy divisions, and Wuloosya has responded by requesting additional international assistance.
President Ironvisak F. Willham opens the folder slowly, reading the documents.

Across the room, Agent Rebecca Kimball steps forward.

Agent Rebecca Kimball
 Our intelligence networks indicate that Rosenmarkke leadership believes Oceanican supplies are already tipping the balance of the conflict. Their state media is portraying us as indirect aggressors.

She pauses before continuing.

If that narrative spreads further, Mr. President, it could justify retaliation, political, economic or worse.

The President leans back in his chair, fingers interlocked.

President Ironvisak F. Willham
 So we send humanitarian supplies and advisors and suddenly we are the enemy.

He looks up sharply.

Tell me something, General. How long before Rosenmarkke decides that volunteers and supply shipments are the same as an army?

General Arthur hesitates for a moment.

General John Arthur
 If the conflict continues to intensify weeks, perhaps days.

A murmur spreads across the officials seated along the sides of the table.

President Willham slowly stands.

President Ironvisak F. Willham
 Then we may already be too late.

The room grows tense again as the President walks toward the large strategic display screen on the wall. 

He turns back toward the council.

Agent Kimball what are they planning next?

Kimball takes a breath before answering.
Agent Rebecca Kimball
 Mr. President our analysts believe Rosenmarkke may be preparing something larger than a border offensive.

The door slides shut behind the arriving officials. Several members of the Enclave 

Representative Council take their seats along both sides of the long briefing table. Each carries folders, tablets, and briefing notes.

President Ironvisak F. Willham slowly walks back toward the head of the table.

President Ironvisak F. Willham
 Since, we have some Enclave Representative Council who have recently joined the meeting, we will continue this discussion with full oversight.

He gestures toward the council members.

General Arthur has informed me that Rosenmarkke is increasing military deployments along the Wuloosyan frontier. Agent Kimball believes their government is preparing to blame Oceanica for escalating the conflict. As well as further requests from Four Agreements, mainly New Westmore and ULR threaten us to stop our support in aid these people.

A man seated near the center of the council table clears his throat.

Council Speaker Daniel K. Harrow
 Mr. President, the council was briefed on the public unrest this morning. Nearly half the population already opposes our involvement overseas. If this turns into open conflict, we will face political instability at home.

Another representative leans forward.

Representative Elena Torres
 The Federal Techno-Democracy policy was meant to stabilize the region, not push us toward war. We need clarity. Are we sending more than supplies and volunteers? And so what, these leaders from Four Agreements try to show power on us?! 

General John Arthur folds his hands behind his back.

General John Arthur
 At this moment, Representative Torres, no official combat units have been deployed. However, Strategic Defense Command has contingency plans prepared should the situation deteriorate.

Murmurs spread across the council seats.

Agent Rebecca Kimball steps toward the central display table. She activates the projection screen, revealing a strategic map of the WuloosyaRosenmarkke sea border.

Agent Rebecca Kimball
 Council members, our intelligence indicates Rosenmarkke leadership believes Oceanica is already interfering directly. Their propaganda networks have begun framing this conflict as resistance against foreign influence.

She zooms

Military build-ups here here and along this corridor suggest preparations for a large scale operation within the next several weeks.

Council Speaker Harrow looks toward the President.

Council Speaker Daniel K. Harrow
 Then we must ask the question directly, Mr. President.

He pauses.

Are we preparing for war?

The room becomes completely silent.

President Ironvisak F. Willham rests his hands on the table, looking across the assembled council members, generals, and intelligence officers.

President Ironvisak F. Willham
I am preparing for every possibility. But I fear we must remain outside this conflict for the sake of national security and to prevent further tension with our allies.

He looks toward General Arthur.
But if this becomes a war it may depend on the decisions we make in this room today.

The Enclave Representative Council members exchange uneasy glances as the strategic map across the wall.

The President takes a slow breath.

President Ironvisak F. Willham
For now, the United States of Oceanica will issue a statement of neutrality. All support operations will be withdrawn. Oceanica will stay out of the conflict.

The room falls silent.[/spoiler]
The government of the United States of Oceanica is closely observing the war between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke.

After holding an emergency security council meeting with the Enclave Representative Council, Strategic Defense Command, and intelligence officers, the President of the United States of Oceanica, Ironvisak F. Willham, has made the final decision regarding the new position of the country on the war between the two nations.

After considering the situation, the views of the Oceanica people, the United States of Oceanica has decided that the country will not take sides in the war between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke. The country will immediately begin withdrawing all the support that the United States of Oceanica had been offering to the region.

The decision of the United States of Oceanica not to take sides in the war between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke is meant to ensure that the war does not intensify, the stability of the world is maintained, and the security of the United States of Oceanica is guaranteed.

The United States of Oceanica appeals to the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke to seek diplomatic meetings and negotiations. The United States of Oceanica supports the efforts of the world towards finding an appropriate solution to the war between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke.

Even though the United States of Oceanica does not support the war between the United Commonwealth of Wuloosya and the Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke through strategic actions, the country will still support the war through the promotion of peace.  

Signed,

Ironvisak F. Willham
President of the United States of Oceanica

[b]The Wuloosyan Rosenmarkket War: Lamentations[/b]

Julian sits alone in the Square Office, two documents on his desk, the resignation of Caleb Roommers and Alwin Rozen. The Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of State, both gone in a day. Dennouncing him publicly as they stormed out. 

"Judas..." He thought

All he could do now was sit here and lament, mulling over feelings of bitterness and defeat. He had felt like this before, after he lost the 2023 election to Hanneke Boshove. Just like in 2023, he seemingly went out of the presidency just like his father, disgraced and a "loser" as Boshove called him during his victory speech. Betrayed by his close allies. After that, he had determined to himself that he wasn't going to go out like his father; he would win the presidency again. He threw his desire for victory and revenge into the building of a new movement, a new movement roomers and Rosen had taken center stage in, now that they were gone, he was right back where he started. He had thrown it all away, and for what? A war that the OSS was now telling him was based on pretenses. Rozen told him this wouldn't end well; he should have listened. 

Suddenly, the buzzer on his office door goes off, and he quickly pushes the button to open it.

"Mr President!" Mary Eikelboom, the now acting Secretary of State says as she enters the office, briefcase in hand

"Oh uh. Eikelboom. Come in." He says, Eikelboom quickly grabs one of the chairs in the offices and sits down in front of the President's desk.

"So I want to thank you again for appointing me as acting Secretary of State. You won't regret it! Anyhow. I've come up with a plan to deal with the international situation" She says, awaiting a response

"Your uh. Welcome, I suppose, and do tell." Julian says, half asleep, at this rate .

"Im sure you're aware that USO just cut support to us and is asking us to seek a peaceful resolution. Similarly, the United Lavinian Republic and New Westmore have also begun to act against us. They all call for some sort of peaceful resolution, so I thought, hey how can we make ourselves look good, right?" She says, grabbing a note sheet out of her briefcase

"So! I just got off the phone with my counterpart in Rosenmarkee, and they're willing to consider a week-long ceasefire! It took alot of convincing, I spent almost 4 hours on the phone with them and some other representative..." She grabs another paper from her desk, Julian picks it up he begins to read it

" [b]CONDITIONS FOR A CEASEFIRE BETWEEN THE UNITED COMMONWEALTH OF WULOOSYA AND THE PEOPLES REPUBLIC OF ROSENMARKEE[/b]

1. Wuloosya and Rosenmarkee will commit to a week-long cessation of armed action against each other.

2. Neither side will violate the other's territorial integrity during this time.

3. Rosenmarkett submarines will be allowed to withdraw unmolested from the combat area of the white sea.

4. Wuloosya will not interfere with humanitarian aid shipments for the duration of the ceasefire and war. The WDF will commit to ensuring humanitarian aid arrives unmolested to Rosenmarkee

5. The Wuloosyan Government will make an effort to limit the participation of the HDF in future operations.

6. The State Department will provide reparations directly to the family of Polnne Strom."

"I know you didn't give me permission to do that, and im sorry, but I hoped you would be impressed nonetheless," She says, ending her presentation

"Actually, this will not be-..." Julian thinks for a moment. Eikelboom is right, this will only improve the image of the war internationally. 

"Hm..."

He has the power to shoot this down, and he doesn't like this deal, esspecially not allowing the Rosenmarket submarines to just escape after all the effort the WDNK has put into chasing them down. But, he can't repeat the same mistake he just made, he already lost Rozen and Roomers. He will not throw away his presidncy for pride, just this once he will...

"Thank you, Secretary. Inform the Rosenmarket that this has my support."

__________________________________________________________________________

The State Department of Wuloosya, after engaging in diplomatic negotiations with several Rosenmarkket repersenatives submits this proposal to its counterpart. As a gesture of goodwill, 10,000,000 dollars is sent over from the National Bank of Wuloosya under the direction of the Department of the Treasury to Rosenmarkee's equivalent to be transferred to the immediate family of Polnne Strom.
